/**
 * Built-in Pi web tools — `web_search` and `web_fetch`.
 *
 * NOT imported by ori's runtime: it ships inside harness-pi and is loaded by the
 * spawned `pi` binary via `--extension <path>`, running in pi's own module graph.
 * `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, `typebox`, `@openrouter/agent`, and
 * `@openrouter/sdk` are devDependencies so ori's typecheck validates against the
 * real APIs. At runtime pi loads it via `jiti`: `@earendil-works/*` and `typebox`
 * resolve from pi's bundled virtual modules, but `@openrouter/agent` is NOT
 * bundled, so its dynamic import below resolves against the filesystem; the harness
 * installs it into a `node_modules` sibling of this materialized file (see
 * `setUpWebToolsExtension` in web-tools-setup.ts). NOTE: this file plus its
 * `web-tools-ssrf.ts` sibling are embedded byte-for-byte as `.ts.txt` twins and
 * materialized side-by-side, so both stay self-contained; the only cross-module
 * import allowed is the relative `./web-tools-ssrf.ts` one below (jiti resolves
 * it from the materialized file).
 *
 * - `web_search` uses the agent SDK's `callModel` with the `web` plugin (runs the
 *   search once per request — the right semantics for a tool named `web_search`,
 *   vs the `web_search` server tool which lets the model decide). Citations come
 *   back as `url_citation` annotations. The SDK import is lazy + guarded.
 *   `ORI_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL`, when set, redirects the client at a key-injecting
 *   proxy (docker's key-proxy) so search authenticates with a placeholder key.
 * - `web_fetch` fetches a URL's text with an SSRF blocklist (private / loopback /
 *   link-local / cloud-metadata) enforced on every redirect hop. The guard checks
 *   the literal host AND every A/AAAA record it resolves to, so a public name that
 *   resolves to an internal IP (DNS-rebinding / dual-record) is blocked.
 */

import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";

import { Type } from "typebox";

import {
  followRedirects,
  htmlToText,
  isBlockedIp,
  pinnedFetch,
  setDnsResolver,
  validateFetchUrl,
} from "./web-tools-ssrf.ts";

// The one env-read site in this file. Bound to the live object rather than
// snapshotted, so every reader below sees the value at call time -- pi hands
// this extension its configuration through the process env, and there is no
// other channel.
// eslint-disable-next-line no-process-env -- pi provides these; reading them is the contract
const extensionEnv = process.env;

const MAX_FETCH_CHARS = 50_000;

const DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS = 5;
const MIN_MAX_RESULTS = 1;
const MAX_MAX_RESULTS = 20;

interface ToolResult {
  content: { type: "text"; text: string }[];
  details: null;
  isError?: boolean;
}

const textResult = (text: string, isError = false): ToolResult => {
  // Omit `isError` on success (callers assert undefined); set it only for errors.
  const result: ToolResult = {
    content: [
      {
        type: "text",
        text,
      },
    ],
    details: null,
  };
  if (isError) {
    result.isError = true;
  }
  return result;
};

const SEARCH_MODEL = "openai/gpt-4o-mini";
const WEB_SEARCH_PLUGIN_ID = "web";

interface ExtractedCitation {
  title: string;
  url: string;
}

interface SearchModelResult {
  getText(): Promise<string>;
  getResponse(): Promise<{
    output: {
      type: string;
      content?: {
        type: string;
        annotations?: { type: string; url?: string; title?: string }[];
      }[];
    }[];
  }>;
}

interface SearchRequest {
  readonly apiKey: string;
  readonly baseUrl: string | undefined;
  readonly query: string;
  readonly maxResults: number;
}

type SearchRunner = (
  request: SearchRequest,
  signal?: AbortSignal
) => Promise<SearchModelResult>;

let searchRunnerOverride: SearchRunner | undefined;

const setSearchRunner = (runner: SearchRunner | undefined): void => {
  searchRunnerOverride = runner;
};

const defaultSearchRunner = async (
  request: SearchRequest,
  signal?: AbortSignal
): Promise<SearchModelResult> => {
  const { apiKey, baseUrl, query, maxResults } = request;
  const { OpenRouter } = await import("@openrouter/agent");
  // `serverURL` is the SDK's base-URL option (Speakeasy naming, not `baseURL`).
  // `undefined` falls back to the SDK's own openrouter.ai default, so every
  // non-proxied deployment keeps its current behaviour.
  const client = new OpenRouter({
    apiKey,
    serverURL: baseUrl,
  });
  // The `web` PLUGIN always searches (runs once per request); see file header.
  const result = client.callModel(
    {
      input: query,
      model: SEARCH_MODEL,
      plugins: [
        {
          id: WEB_SEARCH_PLUGIN_ID,
          maxResults,
        },
      ],
    },
    signal ? { fetchOptions: { signal } } : undefined
  );
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-type-assertion
  return result as unknown as SearchModelResult;
};

type SearchOutputItem = Awaited<
  ReturnType<SearchModelResult["getResponse"]>
>["output"][number];

type SearchOutputPart = NonNullable<SearchOutputItem["content"]>[number];

const partCitations = (part: SearchOutputPart): ExtractedCitation[] => {
  if (part.type !== "output_text") {
    return [];
  }
  return (part.annotations ?? []).flatMap((ann) =>
    ann.type === "url_citation" && ann.url !== undefined
      ? [
          {
            title: ann.title ?? ann.url,
            url: ann.url,
          },
        ]
      : []
  );
};

const messageCitations = (item: SearchOutputItem): ExtractedCitation[] =>
  item.type === "message" ? (item.content ?? []).flatMap(partCitations) : [];

const extractCitations = (
  response: Awaited<ReturnType<SearchModelResult["getResponse"]>>
): ExtractedCitation[] => response.output.flatMap(messageCitations);

const runWebSearch = async (
  query: string,
  maxResults: number,
  signal?: AbortSignal
): Promise<ToolResult> => {
  // `ORI_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` is set only by a deployment that fronts OpenRouter
  // with a key-injecting proxy (docker's key-proxy), where the key above is a
  // placeholder the proxy replaces. Absent, the SDK keeps its own default.
  const { OPENROUTER_API_KEY, ORI_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL } = extensionEnv;
  if (!OPENROUTER_API_KEY) {
    return textResult(
      "Error: OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set in the environment.",
      true
    );
  }
  const trimmedBaseUrl = ORI_OPENROUTER_BASE_URL?.trim();
  const baseUrl =
    trimmedBaseUrl === undefined || trimmedBaseUrl === ""
      ? undefined
      : trimmedBaseUrl;

  const runner = searchRunnerOverride ?? defaultSearchRunner;
  let text: string;
  let citations: ExtractedCitation[];
  try {
    const result = await runner(
      {
        apiKey: OPENROUTER_API_KEY,
        baseUrl,
        maxResults,
        query,
      },
      signal
    );
    text = await result.getText();
    citations = extractCitations(await result.getResponse());
  } catch (error) {
    return textResult(
      `Search failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
      true
    );
  }

  const sourcesSection =
    citations.length > 0
      ? `\n\nSources:\n${citations.map((c, i) => `[${i + 1}] ${c.title}\n    ${c.url}`).join("\n")}`
      : "";

  return textResult(
    `Search results for "${query}":\n\n${text || "(no response text)"}${sourcesSection}`
  );
};

// JSON / plain text bypass htmlToText — stripping would corrupt them.
const renderFetchedBody = async (
  final: Response,
  rawUrl: string
): Promise<ToolResult> => {
  const contentType = final.headers.get("content-type") ?? "";
  const isTextual =
    contentType.includes("text/") ||
    contentType.includes("application/json") ||
    contentType.includes("application/xhtml");
  if (!isTextual) {
    return textResult(
      `URL: ${rawUrl}\nContent-Type: ${contentType}\n(Binary content — not returning body)`
    );
  }

  const raw = await final.text();
  const isHtml =
    contentType.includes("text/html") ||
    contentType.includes("application/xhtml");
  const text = isHtml ? htmlToText(raw) : raw;
  const truncated =
    text.length > MAX_FETCH_CHARS
      ? `${text.slice(0, MAX_FETCH_CHARS)}\n\n[... truncated at ${MAX_FETCH_CHARS.toLocaleString()} chars — ${(text.length - MAX_FETCH_CHARS).toLocaleString()} chars omitted]`
      : text;

  return textResult(
    `URL: ${rawUrl}\nContent-Type: ${contentType}\n\n${truncated}`
  );
};

// `web_fetch` exists to retrieve arbitrary model-chosen URLs, so a deployment
// whose only permitted egress is a key-injecting proxy (docker's key-proxy)
// cannot offer it: covering it would mean letting the proxy forward anywhere,
// which is the open relay the lockdown exists to prevent. A host allowlist was
// considered and rejected -- it needs maintenance, fails unpredictably, and any
// allowlisted host with an open redirect defeats it. When the deployment sets
// this, say so in the description, the prompt snippet AND the tool result,
// because the alternative is the model burning turns on what looks like a flaky
// network. `web_search` is unaffected: it goes through the proxy.
const WEB_FETCH_DISABLED_ENV = "ORI_DISABLE_WEB_FETCH";
const WEB_FETCH_DISABLED_MESSAGE =
  "web_fetch is disabled in this deployment: the agent's only network egress is the OpenRouter key-proxy, so arbitrary URLs cannot be fetched. Use web_search instead.";

// Only the exact string "1" opts in, so an inherited `ORI_DISABLE_WEB_FETCH=0`
// cannot silently remove the tool.
const isWebFetchDisabled = (): boolean =>
  extensionEnv[WEB_FETCH_DISABLED_ENV] === "1";

const runWebFetch = async (
  rawUrl: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal
): Promise<ToolResult> => {
  // Gated here rather than at the registration site so the refusal covers every
  // caller of the tool, not just the one closure pi happens to invoke.
  if (isWebFetchDisabled()) {
    return textResult(WEB_FETCH_DISABLED_MESSAGE, true);
  }
  const validated = await validateFetchUrl(rawUrl);
  if ("error" in validated) {
    return textResult(`Fetch blocked: ${validated.error}`, true);
  }

  let response: Response;
  try {
    response = await pinnedFetch(validated, signal);
  } catch (error) {
    return textResult(
      `Fetch failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
      true
    );
  }

  const redirected = await followRedirects(response, validated.url, signal);
  if ("error" in redirected) {
    return textResult(redirected.error, true);
  }
  const final = redirected.response;

  if (!final.ok) {
    return textResult(
      `Fetch failed (HTTP ${final.status} ${final.statusText}): ${rawUrl}`,
      true
    );
  }

  return await renderFetchedBody(final, rawUrl);
};

// Takes only the slice of pi it uses. `ExtensionAPI` satisfies this, so pi's own
// call is unchanged, and a test can hand it a plain object without a cast.
// eslint-disable-next-line import/no-default-export -- pi loads extensions via default-export factory
export default function register(pi: Pick<ExtensionAPI, "registerTool">): void {
  pi.registerTool({
    name: "web_search",
    label: "Web Search",
    description:
      "Search the web for current information about a company, person, domain, or topic. Use for research, verification, and any query requiring up-to-date information beyond your training data.",
    promptSnippet:
      "web_search(query) - Search the web via OpenRouter for real-time information",
    parameters: Type.Object({
      query: Type.String({ description: "The search query" }),
      max_results: Type.Optional(
        Type.Number({
          description: `Maximum number of results to return (default: ${DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS})`,
          minimum: MIN_MAX_RESULTS,
          maximum: MAX_MAX_RESULTS,
        })
      ),
    }),
    execute: (_toolCallId, params, signal) =>
      runWebSearch(
        params.query,
        params.max_results ?? DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS,
        signal
      ),
  });

  pi.registerTool({
    name: "web_fetch",
    label: "Web Fetch",
    description: isWebFetchDisabled()
      ? WEB_FETCH_DISABLED_MESSAGE
      : "Fetch the full text content of a URL. Use after web_search to read the actual content of a page — company websites, profiles, news articles, registry filings, etc.",
    promptSnippet: isWebFetchDisabled()
      ? "web_fetch(url) - DISABLED in this deployment; use web_search instead"
      : "web_fetch(url) - Fetch and return the text content of a URL",
    parameters: Type.Object({
      url: Type.String({ description: "The URL to fetch" }),
    }),
    execute: (_toolCallId, params, signal) => runWebFetch(params.url, signal),
  });
}

export const __testing = {
  defaultSearchRunner,
  htmlToText,
  isBlockedIp,
  runWebFetch,
  runWebSearch,
  setDnsResolver,
  setSearchRunner,
  validateFetchUrl,
};
export type { SearchModelResult };
